text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Pakistan succeeded in persuading the International Monetary Fund to urgently send a mission to Pakistan on October 24. But a joint statement issued after the talks in Washington confirmed that Islamabad would have to implement a number of "prior actions" before any commitment for release of the suspended $600 million standby loan was made.
- The IMF management has approved almost the same package which the Pakistani team brought for talks and now it is for Islamabad to implement it, Pakistani officials in Washington said.
- The State Department urged U.S. citizens in Pakistan to be careful about their personal security because of what it said was a continuing threat of anti-American violence.
- Iranian Consul General Mohammad Taqi Jamshaidi said his country was keen to export cheap electricity to Pakistan.
- Pakistan plans to devise a "transparent policy" for exports to the Russian Federation.
- The two collectorates of general sales tax of Karachi region have mopped up 1.741 billion rupees at the manufacturing stage in the first quarter (July-September) of the fiscal year.

- The federal and provincial development programmes for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) will be slashed by at least 25 billion rupees to ensure the budgetary deficit is brought down to about four percent of GDP.
- The government may cancel a contract awarded to Britain's National Grid Co after it failed to lay a power transmission line.
- The World Bank has expressed concern over the level of receivables from state-run Water and Power Development Authority consumers which had reached 19.6 billion rupees by May 1996.
- Pakistan Farmers Association said a sharp rise in fertliser prices has jeopardised the achievement of 18.5 million tonnes wheat output target set by the government.
- The United States has decied to impose customs duties on certain Pakistani exports with effect from July 1996, saying Islamabad has not done enough to protect labour rights.
- The presidents of Pakistan and Uzbekistan said peace can only be restored in Afghanistan if a broad coalition government of the main ethnic and political groups is set up.
- The U.S.-Pakistan Defence Consultative Group starts a three-day meeting today.
